tier: historical hosted CI/CD service (end of life)
confidence_note: The end-of-life notices and the historical Shippable documentation are first-party pages captured and quoted. No build was run and no account was opened. The historical build-minute free allowance is not stated on any first-party page read and is unverified.

free_tier.stated: Historical hosted plan: free for all open-source projects and one private project with unlimited builds, stated on a preserved first-party pricing page from 2014. Paid plans were announced as coming soon and the hosted service has since ended; this is not a current offer
free_tier.notes: The preserved page states unlimited builds rather than a build-minute or build-count number, so the nearest unit term is unlimited. The offer is historical and the service no longer runs.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object cap is stated on the pages read; the service ran builds rather than storing objects

retention.stated: unverified: no build or build-log retention period is stated on the pages read

egress.terms: unverified: no egress allowance or per-gigabyte price is stated on the pages read. A self-hosted Server and bring-your-own-node option existed, but no hosted egress figure is established

interface_detail: A connected source-control repository drove builds on the hosted service. A REST API under docs.shippable.com/platform/api described programmatic access; the service has reached end of life. A separately named product at shippable.dev is a code scanner rather than a CI runner and is not this offer.
endpoint: unverified: no current hosted API endpoint remains after the end of life
tooling: A hosted CI/CD platform where the vendor spun up build machines called Minions for each build. A self-hosted Server and bring-your-own-node option existed as secondary choices; neither is the hosted offer documented here.
chaining: A push to a connected GitHub or Bitbucket repository started a build on vendor-run build machines. The product was made part of JFrog Pipelines, which also reached end of life, so this chain no longer runs on Shippable.

limits.value: JFrog Pipelines reached end of life on May 1, 2026, and no longer receives updates, bug fixes, or security patches
a 30 day free pilot license was offered for the self-hosted Shippable Server, not for the hosted runner

limits_note: The hosted free plan stated unlimited builds without a build-minute number; no request-rate or per-object figure was published on the pages read.
binding_note: The successor product's end of life stops new builds for every plan, so discontinuation binds before any historical pilot or build limit.

identity_cost.detail: The hosted service required no separately created account: sign-in used GitHub or Bitbucket credentials through OAuth, which the user authorized on first sign-in. The source-control account therefore carried an email identity. No card or phone requirement is established from the page read and no sign-up was performed

reliability_note: The hosted CI service was acquired and made part of JFrog Pipelines, which reached end of life on May 1, 2026 and no longer receives updates or support.

notes: A hosted CI/CD service that was acquired by JFrog in 2019, made part of JFrog Pipelines and discontinued with that product on May 1, 2026. The current shippable.dev domain serves a code scanner and is a different offer, not a runner. A self-hosted Server and bring-your-own-node option were secondary choices and never the hosted offer.
